headline: Mail reaction to AAPL (margin and Services) and MRVL-LITE keeps tech de-grossed into the midterms; desks still rotate into AMZN and the 'no negative discovery' AI names while shorts build in AMD before its print.
market_read: The de-gross is now quantified: GS Prime (3 Nov) has TMT L/S funds -12.6% in October, US Info Tech long/short ratio at 1.71 (7th percentile over 5 years) and Mag 7 net sold in 4 of 5 sessions, while Vanda (2 Nov, forwarded by Rodrigo Nascimento) has US equity positioning below neutral for the first time since April and CTA NDX exposure flat. Desks disagree on what comes next: UBS (3 Nov) expects Risk Control to turn buyer today after ~$85-115bn of systematic selling, JPM Market Intel stays Tactically Bullish on a tech rebound, but GS's Callahan (2 Nov) describes a 'wait and see' tape where beats go unrewarded in TMT and JPM's Benhamou says long-onlys are still neutral-to-overweight so the incremental buyer is missing. On names, AAPL fell 4% on a 45-46% GM guide and an 8-9% Services guide (JPM, MS, GS), the MRVL-LITE deal was hated across every house we read (BofA downgraded MRVL to Neutral), and the flow story is money leaving MSFT and neoclouds for AMZN and GOOGL, the names that can tap the bond market (JPM TMT desk, Rothschild).

up.why: The most-asked print of the week: JPM's buyside survey still scores +3 but Meyers (3 Nov) says shorts rose materially even before INTC, Barclays (2 Nov) pegs a high-$16bn 4Q guide as the bogey and Jefferies (3 Nov) says $16.5bn is realistic while buyside DC expectations sit at $80-90bn vs Street ~$70bn. Bernstein's Rasgon likes it for CPU exposure. Bloomberg X attention is not spiking yet; the HOT band is 40-<60 (score 44) where this name's own 5-session analog is +1.1% mean, 48% up (n=33), so the print, not attention, decides the next 1-5 days; over 2-4 weeks a reset bar with fresh shorts is the squeeze setup.
up.confirm: DecQ revenue guide at or above $16.5bn with DC revenue qualitatively ahead and server-CPU share commentary intact; shorts cover on the open.
up.weaken: Client guide cut larger than a few hundred million, or DC guide reiterated without upside while PC channel inventory is called out.

up.why: Attention without sponsorship: Bloomberg X z-score 2.03 (change +3.26, 7-day average 120 posts vs 15 baseline) while the stock is -37% over 28 days, and every house read (Bernstein, UBS, BofA, Rothschild, TMTB, Irrational Analysis) dislikes the deal for LITE holders; JPM's survey sits at 0. The HOT band is 60-<80 (score 72.8) where LITE's own 10-session analog is +5.9% mean, 83% up but on only 6 cases, so treat the analog as weak. The 1-5 day driver is the 5 Nov print and spread moves; over 2-4 weeks the name trades as a MRVL proxy.
up.confirm: Spread narrows after the 5 Nov print; JPM's survey moves positive on the standalone guide (Meyers calls it dramatically upbeat).
up.weaken: Spread widens further on regulatory (China/InP) commentary or MRVL keeps falling, dragging the fixed 4.5x ratio value.

up.why: Second day of desks naming AMZN the destination: Rothschild (3 Nov) sees long-only rotation on the multi-year AWS outlook and JPM's TMT desk (2 Nov) saw supportive flows with MSFT as the source of funds; GS's top inbound was 'bounce in AMZN, sustainable?'. Bloomberg X attention is normal and the HOT band is 60-<80 (score 64.2) where AMZN's own 5-session analog is flat (0.0% mean, 43% up, n=7), so the near-term edge is flow, not sentiment; over 2-4 weeks the long-only rotation is the thesis.
up.confirm: Continued desk-flow mentions of LO buying; AMZN holds gains on down tech days as it did 2 Nov (+2.2%).
up.weaken: AI-financing headlines spread to AWS capex funding, or the rotation reverses into a broad AI squeeze that favours semis.

up.why: Sponsorship keeps building: GS added APH to the US Conviction List (2 Nov, 2027 EBITDA 10% above Street) and Barclays raised its PT to $111 (2 Nov). HOT band 60-<80 (score 74) and BULL band 60-<80 (78.1) where APH's own 5-session analog is +5.6% mean, 80% up (n=7, small). Over 2-4 weeks this is the 'non-semis AI winner' crowding candidate; watch for it tipping into excessive popularity.
up.confirm: More houses adding to focus lists; Bloomberg X attention rising with positive tone.
up.weaken: Hardware de-rating catches APH (Barclays notes EMS names down ~24% intra-quarter) or AI-industrials election selling spreads.

up.why: Barclays (2 Nov) said investors hunting for places to hide could come back on solid numbers; the print delivered a slight beat, above-Street 4Q guide and the first AI data-center disclosure ($180mn in 3Q, $620mn 2026) and the stock was +3-4% pre-market (GS, UBS). But TMTB calls it 'not good enough' versus bogeys and JPM's survey was -1, so the desk view is split. No HOT/BULL analog exists for ON; conviction low until a second day of follow-through.
up.confirm: Stock holds the post-print gain and desks report long-only adds on the AI DC disclosure.
up.weaken: Fade on auto supply constraints (down high-single-digits q/q in 4Q) or GM utilization lag disappoints.

down.why: Unanimous dislike after confirmation: -32% on a three-day stack (Rothschild, 3 Nov), BofA's Arya downgraded to Neutral with PO $225 from $400 (3 Nov), Bernstein, UBS and BofA sales all report investors pushing back on price, dilution and approval risk; only Arcuri's bull-case accretion math and the Huang endorsement are on the other side. Bloomberg X attention is up (z 0.85, change +1.61, 374 posts/day vs 147 baseline) with neutral tone and the stock -37% over 28 days; HOT band 40-<60 (score 53.7) where MRVL's own 5-session analog is -1.3% mean, 41% up (n=29). Over 2-4 weeks the overhang is the spread and the 1H28 close.
down.confirm: Further research downgrades or widening spread; no buyer steps in at the fixed ratio.
down.weaken: A collar or revised terms, or a strong LITE standalone guide on 5 Nov that resets the combined EPS case.

down.why: Post-print the 'short-AI haven' narrative cracked: GM guide 45-46% on memory and Siri costs, Services +8-9% (JPM, MS, GS, 2-3 Nov), stock -4% pre-market. Positioning is contested: JPM says shorts were added aggressively into the print, Barclays says positioning had become less negative as investors used AAPL as the anti-semis hedge, and MS saw a safe-haven bid after the call. HOT band 40-<60 (score 54) where AAPL's own 5-session analog is -0.3% mean, 46% up (n=39). Over 2-4 weeks the memory-cost overhang (Barclays: through CY27) replaces the haven trade.
down.confirm: Research PT cuts on GM; the stock fails to hold the post-call bounce and the haven bid moves to other non-AI names (GS list).
down.weaken: Duo supply/demand data strong into the holiday; investors treat the Services guide as one-quarter FX/licensing noise as Meyers argues.

down.why: -7.5% to -8% despite a 13th straight acceleration because forward indicators rolled over: US commercial TCV +11% y/y vs +153%, RDV +79% vs +124%, cRPO 88% vs 105% (GS, 3 Nov), flat RPO for the first time since 1Q23 (UBS). TMTB frames the bear case at ~75x C27 while UBS's Keirstead stays a buyer. No HOT/BULL analog for PLTR. Over 1-5 days the bookings debate dominates; over 2-4 weeks shorter-duration sovereign deals need to show up in revenue to rebuild the premium.
down.confirm: Downgrades citing bookings; the stock breaks below the pre-print level on day two.
down.weaken: Management evidence that short-duration contracts convert faster, or a rebound in US commercial bookings commentary at conferences.

down.why: Financing is now the sorting variable: JPM's TMT desk (2 Nov) says neoclouds that cannot tap the bond market keep selling off, WSJ via TMTB has CoreWeave's 9.75% bonds yielding over 15% and Nebius pulling a high-yield deal, and Rothschild flags ORCL having to pay 7-8.65% coupons. Bernstein's Seidman is the divergent voice: GPU economics supportive, stocks at 52-week lows anyway. Bloomberg X attention is fading (z -0.80, change -1.67, 83 posts/day vs 152 baseline) while the stock is -43% over 28 days, i.e. selling without attention, closer to neglect than capitulation; no analog available.
down.confirm: CRWV/NBIS bonds keep widening; any delayed capacity delivery or lease repricing headline.
down.weaken: A successful asset-backed financing or equity-funded hyperscaler prepayment; AI credit spreads tighten after the midterms.

down.why: A crowded long losing sponsors before the print: Barclays (3 Nov) still calls it very well liked with a 36% growth bogey, but Bernstein's Seidman (2 Nov) says the AI tailwind is priced in and smidcap-software conviction dissipated after NOW/TWLO/FTNT; the stock fell 12% Friday and 8% Monday on the AWS read and CHKP. No HOT/BULL analog. 1-5 days hinge on the print; over 2-4 weeks lighter positioning lowers the bar rather than ending the long.
down.confirm: Desk surveys show long reductions; print reaction muted even on a 36%+ quarter.
down.weaken: Born-in-AI cohort upside (Bernstein's Peter: ~$200M extra ARR) re-crowds the name quickly.

themes.title: De-gross is measured, capitulation is not: what the desks disagree on
themes.text: GS Prime (3 Nov): fundamental L/S -3.5% and TMT L/S -12.6% in October, largest net selling since March, US IT long/short ratio 1.71 (7th pct over 5y). Vanda (2 Nov, via Rodrigo Nascimento): positioning below neutral for the first time since April, CTA NDX exposure flat, retail the only dip buyer. TMTB relays MS PB having hedge funds underweight the AI trade vs market-cap weight for the first time since early 2023. SIG (2 Nov) and JPM's Schlegel still call it a squeeze setup without capitulation because gross stays high. UBS's Cheong turns constructive on flows from Tuesday; JPM Market Intel is Tactically Bullish; GS's Callahan sees 'wait and see'. We weight the flow desks (GS Prime, UBS PB, Vanda) over the strategy calls because they describe what happened rather than what should happen.

themes.title: MRVL-LITE: universal dislike, three different reads on what it signals
themes.text: Every house read the deal negatively for at least one side: BofA downgrades MRVL (Arya), Rothschild and Bernstein report shareholder pushback, TMTB says it has never seen a deal this hated, Irrational Analysis (independent, long semis) expects transceiver OEMs to move DSP business to AVGO/CRDO/SMTC. The disagreement is on the signal: UBS's Vogt reads LITE selling at this point as shortening the AI-cycle duration; Arcuri (same house) models 14% accretion in the LITE bull case; Mizuho (via TMTB) turns it into scarcity-winner longs in AVGO, CRDO and COHR; JPM sees a positive COHR read from LITE's standalone guide. CIEN (-11%) is the collateral name (15% of LITE sales per BofA's Liani).

themes.title: AI financing is the sorting variable: ORCL $20bn, META $20bn, GOOG euro, OpenAI cut, Anthropic 'high junk'
themes.text: JPM's Benhamou (2 Nov) lists the five investor worries: fixed-income capacity, private-equity appetite, equity-market support for ratings, who warehouses idle chips, and the Texas/Nevada governor races. The week answered with ORCL paying 7.00-8.65% coupons plus equity at an 11% discount (Rothschild), S&P negative on META, GOOG paying up in euros, OpenAI cutting its raise to ~$20bn at $1.25tn, and Blackstone expecting Anthropic to be rated high junk post-IPO (Rothschild, 2 Nov). JPM's TMT desk says the names that can borrow (GOOGL) are being bought and the ones that cannot (CRWV, NBIS) sold. Anthropic as a theme: TMTB puts the October ARR bogey at $74-75bn with bulls wanting $78bn+; the S-1/A shows Q3 revenue $16.96bn and ~$895bn of compute commitments (Rothschild, 3 Nov).

themes.title: SemiAnalysis (via Jefferies and UBS) and the election: 2027 build is locked, Texas is the swing
themes.text: SemiAnalysis did not arrive directly in this window; Jefferies (2 Nov) relays its view that ~75% of the 33.8 GW due across the top 20 states is already under construction and the +50 GW global year stands regardless of the midterms, and UBS relays its new agentic benchmark with Google's Carbon near the top. On the election, JPM's Benhamou and UBS both call the Texas governor race (Abbott 61/40 on Kalshi, narrowing) the most consequential for the AI-power trade; Bernstein industrials think the market overprices the risk (~55-60% of the 430 GW pipeline in restriction-leaning states, stable since summer); GS GIR expects the data-center focus to fade after the vote. Desk consensus is that a Blue Wave is priced and the clearing event matters more than the outcome.
